Commentary.Commentary: We are back for New Zealand's reply. The England players are seen having a chit chat near the ropes. They get into a huddle before they disperse and are followed by the two New Zealand openers, Will Young and Devon Conway. Chris Woakes will start the proceedings with the new ball for England. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand will be the happier of the two sides at the halfway mark. The bowlers have vindicated their skipper's decision to bowl first and the onus is now on the batters to finish the job. On the other hand, England were on course for a much bigger total and it would take some bowling effort from them to win from here. Can they succeed in doing so? Back in a bit for the chase...

Glenn Phillips is down for a quick chat. He says that they were brilliant in the field and even though England got off to a flier, they pulled it back in the middle phase and they will take 280. Adds that England were missing Ben Stokes which helped a bit but Tom Latham made good bowling changes. Mentions that the pitch looks good and it will get better but might turn a bit as well which makes it more of an even contest.

After being inserted into bat, England were off to a blazing start, with Jonny Bairstow getting off the blocks in the very first over. After chancing his luck for the first few overs, Dawid Malan eventually departed and was followed back into the hut by Bairstow. As he always does, Harry Brook looked to attack from ball one, but the same approach led to his downfall. Joe Root and Jos then got together and forged a solid recovery for England. During the 70-run stand, Buttler was the aggressor of the two batters, while Root was happy playing the second fiddle. Buttler missed out on a fifty, and it all went downhill for his side from there. They kept losing wickets at regular intervals but thanks to the unbeaten 30-run stand between Adil Rashid and Mark Wood, England have a competitive total on the board.

A decent end to the innings for England but this has been a stunning bowling effort by New Zealand! Considering the bowling resources they had, Tom Latham will be pleased with how things have panned out. Trent Boult was not able to set the tone early, but it was made up for by Matt Henry keeping things quiet from his end. Henry was rewarded for his patience before Mitchell Santner got into the act and removed the other opener. The middle phase was a lull for New Zealand, as it was pretty much dominated by the pair of Joe Root and Jos Buttler. Just when both batters were beginning to flex their muscles, Matt Henry was brought back, and he nipped out the English skipper. It was all New Zealand post that as Tom Latham rotated his bowlers well and they kept chucking away with wickets. Matt Henry was the pick of the bowlers with figures of 3 for 48 from his allotted overs. Mitchell Santner and Glenn Phillips accounted for two wickets each and were impressive in pulling things back for New Zealand.

Ends well does James Neesham and England manage to scrape over the 280-run mark! Full and outside off, in the blockhole. Mark Wood backs away but gets a bottom edge just behind the stumps and Adil Rashid is quick to scamper toward the striker's end. New Zealand aren't in a hurry and Wood too manages to get to the other end. England finish with 282/9!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get going! The two umpires are out in the middle as the Kiwi players take their places on the field as well. It will be the right-hand and left-hand combination of Jonny Bairstow and Dawid Malan to open the innings for England. Trent Boult has the new ball in hand and will be looking to get it to talk early on. Just the one slip in place and here we go...

We are just a few minutes away from take-off in the 2023 Cricket World Cup but first, the two sets of players will line up for their respective national anthems. Before the anthems though, a legend of the game, Sachin Tendulkar walks out and stands beside that coveted trophy. It will be the national anthem of New Zealand first, followed by the national anthem of England.

England's skipper Jos Buttler says that they would have bowled first as well. Mentions that it is a good wicket and they cannot wait to get going. Says that they had a good series against New Zealand and everyone is in a really good place. Shares that they are proud of the achievement in 2019 and are here to attack and win. Informs that Ben Stokes misses out due to a hip niggle. Ends by saying that Gus Atkinson, David Willey, and Reece Topley are the others missing out.

New Zealand skipper, Tom Latham says they will bowl first as it looks a good surface but might get better later on. Adds that the guys have been in different parts of the world and came together a week back and are pumped up. Adds that the series against England in the past month is a big plus as they know what to expect. On Kane Williamson, he says that unfortunately he misses out and hopefully, he will be fit for future games. Also informs that the likes of Tim Southee, Ish Sodhi and Lockie Ferguson all miss out as well.
